correctness.rationale: Writing x=||x||u and y=||y||v gives the stated profile with t=||x||/||y||, and positive scaling preserves Birkhoff orthogonality. For D=tu−t⁻¹v and d=||D||, the orthogonality and reverse triangle inequalities give d≥t and d≥|t−t⁻¹|. For t≤1 the identity u−v=tD+(1−t²)u gives bounds 2t below t=1/√2 and 1/t above it. For t≥1 the identity u−v=t⁻¹D−(1−t⁻²)v gives 2/t−1/t³, maximized at √(3/2) with value 4√6/9<√2. Thus equality forces t=1/√2 and equality in the d lower bound there, i.e. ||u−2v||=1. Conversely the chord is on the sphere by convexity and orthogonality, so ||u−v||=1 and the quotient is √2. The square and diamond witnesses are unit Birkhoff pairs by the indicated norm-one functionals. The lower bound follows from t=1 and a norming functional's nontrivial kernel; Hilbert spaces give exactly 1 since d²=t²+t⁻² for an orthonormal pair. In finite dimension the unit Birkhoff-pair set is closed and compact and the bounds 2/t and 2/|t−t⁻¹| give uniform decay at the two ends. So attainment holds, and strict convexity excludes the required chord.
residual_risks: The strict inequality for strictly convex spaces is proved only in finite dimension; no infinite-dimensional attainment or stability conclusion is certified.

evidence: The unrestricted angular/skew-angular comparison cited by Du et al. supplies a general coefficient 2, not the restricted sharp result. The Filomat paper's MS_B uses max(||x||,||y||) times the angular distance divided by ||x−y||. At x=tu,y=t⁻¹v this ratio is max(t,t⁻¹)Q, not Q; the upper bound 2 there by itself only gives Q≤2 min(t,t⁻¹).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The inspected broader or adjacent constants do not give √2 uniformly and do not establish the sphere-chord equality geometry. The distinct later indexed upper-bound theorem itself is equivalent, not excluded on topical grounds.

originality.rationale: The restricted invariant and the normalized profile are already explicit in Du et al.; the lower sharp endpoint is not new. Their Proposition 2.5 and Example 4.4 explicitly claim sharpness at 2 for the very same restricted invariant. The proved upper bound √2 contradicts that sharpness and the frozen result gives an exact extremizer criterion. A distinct later-published indexed result proves the same √2 bound using the same inequalities in s=t² and includes more ℓ∞ examples; it does not state the pointwise iff, though the iff is obtainable by tracing its sharp endpoint. This is substantive duplication of the theorem, not a different invariant; the catalog entries and the preprint's ambiguous date metadata do not establish an earlier priority for the distinct result. The available earlier statements do not give the claimed sharp comparison. The Pass is for the supported improvement and equality analysis, not certified absolute priority.
residual_risks: Fu–Li's unrestricted angular/skew full text remains inaccessible; an implicit restricted lemma is not ruled out. The time shown in the motivating arXiv first-page header and the apparent identifier month disagree, and indexed dates alone do not establish priority or derivation of the matching result.
